2607.25961.title: Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Reasoning over Interacting Streams for Video-Level Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition
2607.25961.paper_summary: Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are conflicting affective states that precede the delay or abandonment of health behaviour change. Recognition of A/H at the video level is difficult, since the signal arises from disagreement across and within facial, vocal, linguistic, and bodily modalities, and manifests differently across individuals. The proposed PRISM-AH (Predictive Reasoning over Interacting Streams for Multimodal Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition), is a framework that treats A/H as a multimodal conflict that unfolds over time. Frozen vision, audio, and text encoders are aligned into short time windows and passed to a lightweight streaming model that scores cross-modal dissonance, predicts each next window to expose a hesitation surprise signal, discovers behaviour prototypes, and is conditioned on participant metadata. Dense window-level annotations supervise the model as an auxiliary objective, and the decision threshold is calibrated for macro F1. A knowledge-guided large language model then reasons over structured evidence using the expert cue taxonomy of the dataset, and its verdict is fused late only when validation performance improves. On the labelled public test partition of 525 videos, PRISM-AH attains a macro F1 of 0.6133, compared to the reported zero-shot baseline of 0.2827. The reasoning gain is validated to transfer from validation to the larger test partition.
2607.25961.paper_summary_zh: 模糊性和猶豫性（A/H）是導致健康行為改變延遲或放棄的相互矛盾的情感狀態。 在視頻層面識別A/H是困難的，因為信號來自於面部、聲音、語言和身體模態之間及內部的不一致，並且在不同個體中表現不同。 提出的PRISM-AH（多模態模糊性/猶豫性識別的互動流預測推理）是一個將A/H視為隨時間展開的多模態衝突的框架。 凍結的視覺、音頻和文本編碼器被對齊到短時間窗口並傳遞到一個輕量級的流模型，該模型對跨模態不和諧進行評分，預測每個下一個窗口以揭示猶豫驚訝信號，發現行為原型，並基於參與者的元數據進行調整。 密集的窗口級註釋作為輔助目標監督模型，並且決策閾值經過宏觀F1的校準。 然後，知識引導的大型語言模型使用數據集的專家提示分類法對結構化證據進行推理，並且只有在驗證性能改善時才會進行後期融合。 在標記的公共測試分區525個視頻中，PRISM-AH達到了0.6133的宏觀F1，相比之下報告的零樣本基線為0.2827。 推理增益經過驗證可以從驗證轉移到更大的測試分區。
